To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hepatocellular transf ferrin receptor expression is absent in severe secondary siderosis, but that this phenomenon is not related to the degree of iron overload.

hepatocellular expression of the transferrir receptor is present in most cases with secondary siderosis and that the proportion of cases in which the transferrin receptors disappear from the parenchymal cells increases in parallel with the severity of the iron overload.
in secondary siderosis the hepatocellular expression of the transferrir receptor is reduced with increasing hepatocellular and/or Kupffer cellular iron overload.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of hepatocellular and nonparenchymal transfertin receptors in secondary siderosis and the regulation of their expression.
the regulation of the expression of hepatocellular and/or Kupffer cells transferrin receptor by iron.
the behaviour of hepatocellular iron uptake in iron overload diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in secondary siderosis the transferrin receptors disappear from the hepatocytes with increasing iron load, and that this is not related to the disappearance of the epidermal receptor.
the transferrin receptors are expressed in hepatocytes of most cases of secondary siderosis.
the hepatocellular expression of the transferrins receptor is not regulated by the degree of parenchyma iron load, but by other factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in secondary siderosis the transferrin receptors disappear from the hepatocytes when the iron deposition exceeds a certain threshold.
hepatocellular transfervin receptor immunoreactiveity is absent in severe iron overload, but may still be present even in cases of moderate to severe iron deposition.
hepatocellular transferring receptor expression is present in secondary siderosis, but its expression is reduced in cases with high hepatocellular iron loads.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of hepatocellular iron receptors is regulated by iron load.
the transferrin receptors are present in iron overload, and that the presence of the receptors does not correlate with the severity of the iron overload.
